account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment schedule. I attended morning office hours, inspected the mill's sale stock around ten, went home for lunch, and returned for council letters at thirteen. The mill stall held 98 hay blocks, but I did not obtain a clear report about milling operations. The secretary says no correspondence or council business has arrived.

The unusual matter is a repeated, unclear report about a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 21 and others repeated it; one account named the baker, freight, and innkeeper as present. I have neither witnessed a change nor heard a specific proposal, purpose, or decision from those involved. My neighbour crossed the bridge without trouble and likewise regarded the reports as unconfirmed. I tried asking the baker when he passed the office, but he apparently did not hear me. I cannot yet tell whether this concerns transport arrangements, a proposed change, or merely confused gossip.

The baker has advertised bread baked this morning at one emerald per loaf. Otherwise business seems ordinary from what I have observed. My neighbour expects me for tea at fifteen hundred at the dockside cottage. I am due back at the office at sixteen thirty. The innkeeper has confirmed meeting me there at seventeen forty-five before our eighteen hundred great-hall meeting about the inn's service to town. That is a confirmed engagement, unlike the bakery rumours; I do not know whether the two matters are connected.
